text:
hao: quick sync — ran the workload classifier sweep against prod trace sample this morning. results and oddities below
ashwin: awesome, paste the short summary pls.
jess: curious about decode-rate buckets specifically, saw some tail lately.
hao: TL;DR: classifier split by prompt_len + decode_rate reduces batching variance, but kernel selection path hit a regression on the long-slow bucket (prompt>1024, decode_rate<1) — p99 latency +18% vs baseline.
maria: ugh. which kernel? cuda-fft? cu-attn?
hao: looks like the autoselect picked the fused-attn-v2 kernel on that bucket. profiling shows higher memmovetime when KV prefetch is active.
bench-bot: perf summary attached — sample size 4k requests; buckets: short-fast (0-64, >4 tok/s), mid (64-256, 1-4 tok/s), long-slow (256+, <1 tok/s). p50/p95/p99 reported.
ashwin: did the batcher form different batch sizes for long-slow? iirc we cap token-budget lower for that class.
hao: yes, token_budget_ms lowered from 120ms->80ms for long-slow, which reduced avg batch size but increased kernel churn for big models (kv reattach cost).
jess: can you drop the relevant logs? the decode-rate classifier thresholds used?
hao: sure — current classifier config snippet:
```
classifier: 
  prompt_buckets: [0,64,256,1024]
  decode_rate_buckets: [0.9,4.0] # boundaries in tokens/sec
  token_budget_ms: {short:50,mid:90,long:80,xl:140}
  kernel_policy: {prefer_low_mem: false, prefer_throughput: true}
```
maria: interesting — kernel_policy preferring throughput might pick kernels that are bad on sparse kv cache hits. can we add a quick rule: if kv_prefetch_ratio>0.5 and prompt_len>1024, prefer_low_mem=true?
ashwin: sounds reasonable. do we have a metric for kv_prefetch_ratio at request time?
bench-bot: kv_prefetch_ratio is emitted by runtime per request (kv_prefetch_hits / kv_prefetch_attempts). median for long-slow was 0.62 in the sweep.
ashwin: then rule makes sense. also we should try increasing token_budget_ms for long-slow from 80->120 to reduce batch churn and amortize kernel setup. maybe trade some latency for throughput.
hao: tried a local A/B: raising budget to 120 reduced kernel handoffs by ~40% and p99 improved back near baseline, but p50 regressed slightly (~+6ms).
jess: that's acceptable if p99 saves customers. are there memory pressure implications?
hao: marginal — peak GPU memory increased ~2% for those traces. not critical on our Dedicated shapes.
maria: on private deploys with tight memory we need fallback. propose: dynamic rule ordering: 1) if mem_util>85% then prefer_low_mem, else apply decode-rate/prompt rules.
ashwin: good. who will implement? @hao can you submit a small runtime tweak + unit tests. i'll add a rollout plan to console that pins rule to 10% canary.
hao: will do. PR target EOD. will include microbench results and config diff.
ashwin: add an eval prompt set for the long-slow cohort so Optimize can alert if generation quality/regression occurs.
ess: (typo) — ignore
bench-bot: profiling artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/batcher/1799908765/; includes perf flamegraphs and kernel counters.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled? no prod changes until PR + canary.
maria: follow-ups: 1) patch classifier rule (hao) 2) canary + console rollout (nashwin) 3) add long-slow eval set (jess) 4) add mem_util fallback (maria).
hao: assigned. will ping when PR is ready. :thumbsup:
jess: thanks — also let's add a small dashboard panel showing kernel selection distribution by bucket. helped me debug last time.
hao: good call. i'll add that to the PR checklist.
ashwin: ok great sync. if anyone sees other weird p99 spikes, drop a short thread here.
